## Run `run_20261115T155359Z_s20` — headline results

**Records analysed:** 759 (stride 20, 2016-03-18T02:09:17Z → 2016-03-26T00:59:44Z, i.e. 3.314 % of the full time window; all 759 records had status `ok`).

**Anomalous records:** 57 records with |robust z| > 5 (top z = 30.92 on 2016-03-23T20:50:17Z, driven by `max_sta_lta`).

**DAS detections:** 62 detections in 53 records; relative b = 0.9849 (Aki MLE on DAS relative magnitudes), 34 detections above the relative Mc (−0.849).

**Context:** pumping over the 15.96-day deployment window was net negative — 4.654e+05 m³ injected vs 5.059e+05 m³ extracted, net −4.048e+04 m³. The LBNL/NCEDC catalogue (GDR 859, March 2016) contains only 5 events, ML −0.48 to 0.07.

### CALIBRATED estimate — catalogue-based (Shapiro et al. 2021, Eq. 5), LBNL catalogue magnitudes

| b | Sigma | P(Mw ≥ 5.5)/yr | P(Mw ≥ 5.5) over observed volume | P(Mw ≥ 3)/yr |
|---|-------|----------------|-----------------------------------|---------------|
| 1.0 | −5.449 | 1.20e-04 | 5.24e-06 | 0.0372 |
| 0.73 | −5.319 | 4.92e-03 | 2.16e-04 | 0.281 |
| 0.65 | −5.281 | 1.47e-02 | 6.48e-04 | 0.465 |

This is the **calibrated** probability: it uses the LBNL catalogue with proper local magnitudes and completeness (Mc = −0.48), so even at the low b = 0.65 scenario a Pohang-class Mw ≥ 5.5 event is ~1.5 %/yr at the observed injection rate — and only ~6.5e-04 over the observed injected volume.

### UPPER BOUND — DAS-based, uncalibrated magnitudes

b = 0.9849, Sigma = −2.698, **P(Mw ≥ 5.5)/yr = 0.0784** (7.84 %/yr; 0.0024 over the observed volume).

This is the **upper bound**: DAS detections carry only relative, uncalibrated magnitudes and every detection is counted as an event at or above the catalogue Mc, so it **over-counts** — it should not be read as a calibrated hazard estimate, only as a ceiling.

**Bottom line:** the calibrated (LBNL catalogue) estimate puts P(Mw ≥ 5.5) at 1.2e-04 to 1.5e-02 per year across the b scenarios, while the DAS-based upper bound is 0.078/yr. The DAS anomalies (57 records, 62 detections) show transient activity during the March 2016 deployment, but under net-negative (extraction-dominated) pumping and with only 5 small catalogue events, the calibrated likelihood of a Pohang-like Mw ≥ 5.5 remains low.
